problems.title: Fractional part of a negative number
problems.question: Find $\{-1-\sqrt2\}$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: $-3<-1-\sqrt2<-2$, so its floor is $-3$.
The fractional part is $-1-\sqrt2+3=2-\sqrt2$.

problems.title: A floor equation
problems.question: How many solutions satisfy $\lfloor(4x-9)/11\rfloor=x$?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The right side must be an integer. The bounds give $11x\le4x-9<11x+11$, or $-20/7<x\le-9/7$.
The only integer is $x=-2$.

problems.title: Negative powers and fifth roots
problems.question: Simplify $[(a^{-1}+2^{-1})(a+2)^{-1}\sqrt[5]{a^{13}}]/[0.5\sqrt[5]{a^4(\sqrt[5]{a^{-20}})^{-1}}]$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The linear factors reduce to $1/(2a)$. Also $\sqrt[5]{a^{-20}}=a^{-4}$, whose inverse is $a^4$.
The denominator is $(1/2)\sqrt[5]{a^8}$. The quotient is $\sqrt[5]{a^{13}}/[a\sqrt[5]{a^8}]=\sqrt[5]{a^5}/a=1$.

problems.title: Two real roots of a radical equation
problems.question: Find the sum of squared solutions of $\sqrt{x^5\sqrt[3]x}-\sqrt{x^5/\sqrt[3]{x^7}}=240$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Only $u=16$ is positive, giving $|x|=16^{3/4}=8$. The solutions are $\pm8$ and the squared sum is $64+64=128$.

problems.title: An odd auxiliary function
problems.question: $g(x)=f(x)+x^2$ is odd and $f(-5)=1$. Find $f(5)$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.

problems.title: Sum an odd periodic function
problems.question: $f$ is odd with period 6 and $f(x)=3x-x^2$ on $[0,3]$. Find $f(1)+\cdots+f(100)$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The values for residues $1,2,3,4,5,6$ are $2,2,0,-2,-2,0$, whose sum is zero.
The first 96 terms form 16 full periods. Terms 97–100 give $2+2+0-2=2$.

problems.title: Symmetry of a parabola
problems.question: $f$ is quadratic and $f(-10)=f(2019)$. Which listed value equals $f(199)$?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Equal quadratic values occur at inputs symmetric about the vertex axis.

problems.title: Lattice points on a rational graph
problems.question: How many integer-coordinate points lie on $y=(3|x|-2)/(|x|-1)$?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: For integer $x$, $y$ is an integer only when the integer denominator $|x|-1$ divides 1. It must be $1$ or $-1$.
This gives $|x|=2$ or 0, so the points are $(2,4),(-2,4),(0,2)$.

problems.title: Coordinates on an inverse graph
problems.question: $y=(x-1)^2$ is restricted to $x\ge1$. The point $(a,4)$ lies on its inverse graph. Find $a$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Inverse graphs interchange input and output coordinates.
steps: Thus $(4,a)$ lies on the original graph. Substitute $x=4$: $a=(4-1)^2=9$.

problems.title: An equation with infinitely many solutions
problems.question: For which listed $a$ does $||x-1|-1|=x+a$ have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The whole ray $x\ge2$ solves the equation when $a=-2$.
On the other linear pieces the slopes are either $-1$ or, on $[0,1]$, $1$ with intercept 0. Thus $a=0$ also gives infinitely many solutions on $[0,1]$, but is not listed.
problems.note: The full parameter set is {−2,0}; the quiz asks which of the listed values works.

problems.title: Exactly five roots with nested absolute values
problems.question: Find $a$ for which $|x^2-4|x|-5|=a$ has five distinct real solutions.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Set $t=|x|\ge0$. Each positive $t$ gives two $x$ values; $t=0$ gives one.
steps: Five roots require a solution at $t=0$, because all nonzero roots come in opposite pairs. At $t=0$, the left side is 5, so necessarily $a=5$.
For $a=5$, solve $t^2-4t-5=5$ or $-5$. The nonnegative roots are $2+\sqrt{14},4,0$.
These give two pairs and zero, exactly five roots.

problems.title: Even functions and their domains
problems.question: Count the even functions among $x^2,-x^3,(x-1)/(x-1),-|x|,\sqrt{x-1},2x-10$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Evenness requires a domain symmetric about 0 and $f(-x)=f(x)$.
steps: $x^2$ and $-|x|$ are even. The cubic and linear functions fail the value test.
The rational expression is 1 only on its original domain, which excludes 1 but includes $-1$; hence its domain is not symmetric. The square-root domain is not symmetric either.
problems.note: If the rational expression is replaced by its continuous extension at 1, that new function is even. The printed expression itself retains the excluded input.

problems.title: A parabola meets an absolute-value diamond
problems.question: Count solutions of $|x|+|y|=1$, $x=y^2-1$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Substitution gives $1-y^2+|y|=1$, or $|y|(1-|y|)=0$.
Thus $y=0,1,-1$, with corresponding $x=-1,0,0$.

problems.title: Integer inputs in a radical domain
problems.question: How many integers are in the domain of $x/\sqrt{3-|x|}-1/(x+2)$?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The interval is $(-3,3)$ with $-2$ removed. Its integer inputs are $-1,0,1,2$.

problems.title: Integer outputs of a rational function
problems.question: How many integers belong to the range of $48/(x+9/x)$?
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: For $x>0$, $x+9/x$ ranges over $[6,\infty)$; for $x<0$, over $(-\infty,-6]$.
Thus the output range is $[-8,0)\cup(0,8]$. The integers are $-8,\ldots,-1$ and $1,\ldots,8$.

problems.title: Area from trapezoid diagonals and bases
problems.question: A trapezoid has diagonals 6 and 8 and bases 2 and 8. Find its area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Its diagonal vectors can be arranged as two sides of a triangle whose third side is the sum of the bases; $S=d_1d_2\sin\theta/2$.
steps: The sum of bases is 10. Since $6^2+8^2=10^2$, the two diagonals are perpendicular.
Therefore the area is $6\cdot8/2=24$.

problems.title: A parallel segment and triangle areas
problems.question: $BM:MC=3:1$, $MN\parallel AB$ with $N$ on $AC$. Find $[ABC]/[AMN]$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Triangle $CAM$ has area $[ABC]/4$. Triangle $CMN$ has area $[ABC]/16$.
Their difference is $[AMN]=3[ABC]/16$.

problems.title: Area of a tangential right trapezoid
problems.question: A right trapezoid has incircle radius 5 and its longer leg is 16. Find its area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: $h=2r$; sum of bases equals sum of legs; $S=(a+b)h/2$.
steps: The perpendicular leg equals the height, 10. The other leg is 16, so the base sum is $10+16=26$.
The area is $26\cdot10/2=130$.
problems.note: The Georgian condition gives the longer leg, not the longer base.

problems.title: Perpendicular medians determine an area
problems.question: $AC=3,BC=4$, and medians from $A,B$ are perpendicular. Find $[ABC]$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: For vectors $u=CA,v=CB$, perpendicular medians give $(v-2u)\cdot(u-2v)=0$; $S=\tfrac12\sqrt{|u|^2|v|^2-(u\cdot v)^2}$.
steps: Expand the dot product: $5u\cdot v-2(9+16)=0$, so $u\cdot v=10$.
The area is $\tfrac12\sqrt{9\cdot16-100}=\sqrt{11}$.

problems.title: Area of a convex pentagon
problems.question: In convex $ABCDE$, $BC=CD=AE=3$, $AB+DE=3$, and $ABC=CDE=90^\circ$. Find its area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Put $AB=x$ and $DE=3-x$, with $0<x<3$. Triangles $ABC,CDE$ have total area $3x/2+3(3-x)/2=9/2$.

Triangle $ACE$ has sides $\sqrt{9+x^2},\sqrt{9+(3-x)^2},3$. These are exactly the sides of a triangle with base 3, altitude 3, and foot dividing the base into $x,3-x$. By side-side-side congruence its area is $9/2$.
Add the three triangle areas to obtain 9.

problems.title: Check the stated altitude and centroid
problems.question: $AB=BC=5,AC=6$. The bisector from $A$ meets the altitude from $B$ at $K$; $M$ is the centroid. Find $[AKM]$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Angle-bisector theorem; centroid coordinates are averages; coordinate triangle area is half a determinant.
steps: Choose $A=(0,0),C=(6,0),B=(3,4)$. The altitude from $B$ is $x=3$. The bisector from $A$ meets $BC$ in ratio $5:6$, at $(48/11,24/11)$, so its line is $y=x/2$.
Therefore $K=(3,3/2)$ and $M=(3,4/3)$. Their distance is $1/6$, and $A$ is distance 3 from their vertical line.
The area is $\tfrac12\cdot3\cdot(1/6)=1/4$.
problems.note: The printed B-altitude and centroid conditions do not produce any listed answer. The calculation follows those conditions without substituting a different vertex.

problems.title: Area inside a rhombus
problems.question: $M$ is the midpoint of $CD$ in rhombus $ABCD$; $BM$ meets $AC$ at $K$. Find $[AKMD]$ if $AK=20,KM=6.5$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: Rhombus diagonals are perpendicular and bisect each other; Pythagoras; determinant area.
steps: Put $A=(0,-a),C=(0,a),B=(-b,0),D=(b,0)$. Then $M=(b/2,a/2)$ and intersection $K=(0,a/3)$.

problems.title: Midpoints and intersecting segments in a trapezoid
problems.question: $N,M$ are midpoints of legs $AB,CD$; $AM,DN$ meet at $K$. Given $[AKD]=9,[MKD]=6$, find $[ABC]$.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: Write $t=AK/AM$. Triangles $AKD,MKD$ have areas in ratio $t:(1-t)=9:6$, so $t=3/5$.
To derive the parameter relation, put $A=(0,0),D=(d,0),B=(u,h),C=(u+c,h)$. Equating $K=tM=D+t(N-D)$ gives $t(c+3d)=2d$. Thus $c=d/3$.
The height of $K$ is $th/2=3h/10$. Hence $9=[AKD]=3dh/20$, giving $dh=60$. Finally $[ABC]=ch/2=dh/6=10$.

problems.title: Altitude ratios reverse side ratios
problems.question: Triangle altitudes have ratio $3:4:6$, and perimeter is 18. Find its shortest side.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
formulas: For the same area, side length is inversely proportional to its altitude.
steps: The side ratio is $1/3:1/4:1/6=4:3:2$. Nine ratio units total 18, so each is 2.
The shortest side has two units, hence length 4.

problems.title: Area from hypotenuse and inradius
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse 8 and inradius 1. Find its area.
problems.idea: Apply the stated relations and retain any domain restrictions.
steps: The area is $1\cdot9=9$.
